metadata.note: The Chautauqua Lake Railway ran 23 miles up the EAST shore of Chautauqua Lake from Jamestown to Mayville, opening on July 25, 1887 with trackage rights over 1.2 miles of the Buffalo, New York & Philadelphia into Mayville itself. It was formed by the December 29, 1886 merger of the Jamestown Short Line Railway (incorporated May 24, 1886) and the Westfield & Chautauqua Railway (organised April 10, 1886). Of roughly 21 stations only six were ever permanently staffed - Jamestown, Bemus Point, Dewittville, Hartfield, the W.N.Y.&P. Junction and Mayville; the rest were flag stops, a shack or a platform or sometimes just a road crossing where you waved a flag to stop the train. At Mayville it met the Mayville Extension Railroad, which ran 3.5 miles down the WEST shore to the Chautauqua Assembly Grounds, the summer institution that generated most of the lake's passenger traffic. The company was reorganised repeatedly - Jamestown & Lake Erie Railway (October 17, 1894), Jamestown & Chautauqua Railway (January 1, 1899), Jamestown, Chautauqua & Lake Erie Railway (chartered September 25, 1900, which built the 11.25-mile extension north from Mayville to Westfield) - until the Jamestown, Westfield & Northwestern Railroad took over on December 8, 1913, electrified the whole thing at 11,500 V AC stepped down to 650 V DC, and began interurban service on August 20, 1914 with cars lettered 'America's Scenic Route'. A 1941 timetable shows six trips a day each way, three hours apart from 6am to 9pm, timed to meet New York Central trains at Westfield. Passenger service ended on November 30, 1947; diesel freight carried on until the last run on January 21, 1950 and the line was abandoned that year.

geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap route relation 3732640, 'Jamestown, Westfield, and Northwestern Trolley' (34 member ways), pulled in full from the OSM API and routed by Dijkstra shortest path. The relation describes the ELECTRIC-era line; it is used here for the 1887 steam-era Chautauqua Lake Railway on the basis that the JW&NW was the CLR's direct corporate successor over the same roadbed - the JW&NW's station list (Jamestown, Colburns, Phillips Mills, Bemus Point, Maple Springs, Dewittville, Pt. Chautauqua, Hartfield, Mayville) is the CLR's station list.

Jamestown-Mayville: 33.06 km / 20.5 miles traced against a documented 23 miles, of which 8.51 km (26%) is straight-line bridging. Almost all of that is ONE contiguous unmapped gap of about 7.4 km between roughly 42.1377,-79.3635 and 42.1912,-79.4177 - the Bemus Point and Maple Springs stretch, where the lake narrows and the right of way is built over; OSM has nothing there of any kind. The remaining bridges are 0.27 km at Point Chautauqua and 0.55 km at Mayville. Because the gap is bridged with a straight line, the traced total comes out shorter than the real 23-mile route.
Mayville-Westfield: 15.89 km / 9.9 miles against a documented 11.25 miles, 100% real-traced with ZERO straight-line approximation.
The eastward spur out of Jamestown (OSM way 280941304, toward Falconer) is a relation member but is excluded from the through route.

WARNING for anyone re-tracing this corridor: a first attempt built from loose bbox-selected abandoned ways silently produced a route that crossed the lake to the WEST shore and back. Those unnamed ways (77721199, 77721220, 77721227, 77721235, 77721239, 1424775243 and others) belong to OSM relation 1179218, the 'Chautauqua Traction' - a SEPARATE west-shore electric interurban abandoned in 1926. Only the relation 3732640 member ways are used here. Note also that OSM way 76297101 is tagged 'Westfield-Johnstown Trolley', which appears to be a typo for Westfield-Jamestown; it IS a member of relation 3732640 and is correctly part of this line.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequencies before 1941; the pre-1941 headways below are estimated and unsourced (the 1941 six-trips-each-way figure is sourced and is used directly). The Mayville-Westfield section's OPENING year is not sourced - only its September 25, 1900 charter is - so 1902 is used as an inferred construction date. The Mayville Extension Railroad (chartered June 4, 1881, operated July 20, 1881, 3.5 miles from Mayville down the WEST shore to the Chautauqua Assembly Grounds) is NOT traced here: on that side of the lake its alignment cannot be reliably separated in OSM from the Chautauqua Traction interurban that later ran the same shore. One source also gives the Chautauqua Lake Railway an organisation date of July 29, 1885, which is inconsistent with its stated formation from companies incorporated in 1886 and merged December 29, 1886; the 1886 merger is used here.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
